① Face detection (Viola-Jones framework, Ch.11): Haar rectangular features + integral image for O(1) region sums + AdaBoost feature selection + cascade classifier (early stages quickly reject non-face windows). OpenCV cv::CascadeClassifier scans multi-scale with scaleFactor=1.1 and minNeighbors=5 de-duplication.
② Illumination adaptation: histogram equalization is applied to every frame before detection to cope with the dramatic lighting of war-movie scenes.
③ Temporal smoothing: boxes across adjacent frames are associated by IoU (threshold 0.3) and moving-averaged to suppress per-frame jitter, so boxes follow faces smoothly during playback.
④ Playback sync: MediaPlayer plays the original video while the overlay looks up the nearest analyzed frame's boxes by playback position (refreshed every 33 ms) — detection is decoupled from playback for smoothness.
⑤ Performance: 1920×858 → 640×286 working resolution + software decoding frame by frame, meeting the document's ≥10fps processing requirement.
⑥ Search with current frame: at any playback moment the current picture can be captured as the query frame (converted to a luma plane in the same feature space as keyframes), then the keyframe index is reused to retrieve similar moments by comprehensive similarity with one-tap jump — for inspecting face recognition at similar moments.

At any moment during playback, tap \"Search With Current Frame\": the current picture is captured as the query frame, similar moments are found by comprehensive similarity, and tapping a result jumps playback there so you can inspect face recognition at each moment.

① Keyframe extraction & indexing (Ch.10 §10.5): the video is decoded frame by frame in software and 12 keyframes are uniformly sampled — keyframes represent the video content, reducing retrieval scale from per-frame to shot level. Each keyframe is downsampled to width 320, from which a 64-bin brightness histogram (color feature, L1-normalized) and an 18-bin Sobel gradient-orientation histogram (texture feature, magnitude-weighted) are extracted with its timestamp — that completes the index.
② Query-frame retrieval: tap a keyframe as the query frame; its feature is compared with every indexed keyframe by comprehensive similarity, and the Top-5 are returned in descending order.
③ Comprehensive similarity = w_c·histogram intersection (color) + w_t·cosine (texture), w_c=0.6, w_t=0.4, ∈[0,1] — brightness distribution is the primary feature and edge texture complements it, resolving the ambiguity of a single feature.
④ Tap a result row to seek the player to that keyframe's timestamp, visually verifying "locating similar content".

How It Works: Tracking Hit Rate

① Concept (a temporal extension of the tracking hit rate trackRate in "video image recognition"): measures the proportion of frames in which the target is continuously tracked.
② Definition: for adjacent frame pair (i-1, i), the pair is a candidate if frame i-1 has detected faces (target present); it is a hit if frame i contains a box associated (IoU > 0.3) with any box of frame i-1 (target continuously tracked).
③ Tracking hit rate = hit pairs / candidate pairs. Target disappearance or over-large inter-frame displacement (association failure) both count as lost — mirroring the template-tracking rule that trackScore < 0.5 means lost.
④ Auxiliary metrics: longest continuous tracking segment (stability) and average association IoU of hit pairs (association quality).
